clue.text: Pillar where water is drawn from river

parts.note: household water is drawn from the mains supply
the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: A column stands on the bank where people draw water from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: a chief support, like a pillar, someone or something everything else rests on.

clue.text: Tree doctors aboard train heading north

indicators.note: the doctors are riding on board, so they sit inside the other piece
in a down clue, heading north means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it
MO, medical officer, is a doctor; MOS is the plural

explanation.surface: Medics travel on a train going up north past a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' is the verb, as in training a gun; 'heading north' reads it upwards, and 'aboard' puts the doctors inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the acacia known for fluffy yellow flowers is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Introduce trendy source of booze — only one left

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: of the pair of L's (left), just one is kept, so the other is dropped

parts.note: a still is where spirits are distilled

explanation.surface: Someone launches a fashionable distillery with only one bottle remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only one left' drops one of the two L's of STILL, leaving STIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to put an idea gradually into someone's mind is to introduce it.

clue.text: Material traditional in film

parts.note: stock, as in a stock phrase, means standard or customary
E.T. is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: A costume fabric of a classic sort appears in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a stretchy knitted fabric used for bandages and underwear is a material.

clue.text: Oscar joins team after a vote for historic mission

indicators.note: the Oscar and team pair is placed after the vote in the answer

parts.note: a poll is a vote
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a football or cricket team is an eleven

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner joins a team after a vote, for a famous expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sends Oscar and the team behind the vote; the 1969 Moon landing is the mission.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the 1969 American spaceflight that first landed people on the Moon was a historic mission.

clue.text: Menial daughter, one booked by Dickens

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel, so he is put in a book

explanation.surface: A servant girl, a daughter, is written into a novel by Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' means put into a book: Barnaby Rudge is a Dickens title.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a menial, used as a noun, is a servant doing dull, lowly work.

clue.text: Old force guarding province, symbolically described

indicators.note: the police force surrounds the province, as if standing guard round it

parts.note: the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province

explanation.surface: A former police force protects a region, described in symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police until 2001; Northern Ireland is often called the Province.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in the ancient Germanic alphabet of runes is set down in symbols, hence symbolically described.

clue.text: Party guest finds place for a nap beside river

parts.note: a dorm, dormitory, is a room for sleeping
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A party-goer finds somewhere to snooze next to a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The guest is the sleepy one at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland; the Ouse is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion: the drowsy rodent at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Lewis Carroll's story is a famous party guest.

clue.text: Consent obtained in Beeb, essentially, for protection from glare

indicators.note: the consent and the obtaining are placed in the middle of the other piece
the essence of the word is its middle, so the inner letters of Beeb are taken

parts.note: yes gives consent
had means got or obtained

explanation.surface: Permission is secured at the BBC to film something about protection from glare.
explanation.walkthrough: Beeb is the BBC's nickname; 'essentially' keeps its middle pair, and 'in' places consent plus obtained between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor worn on the forehead to shield sight from bright light is a protection from glare.

clue.text: Head of oldest and most outlandish prehistoric beast

indicators.note: outlandish means bizarre, so the letters take a strange new order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The leader of the oldest, strangest creatures from prehistory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlandish' rearranges O (Head of oldest) with AND and MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an extinct elephant-like animal with huge tusks is a prehistoric beast.

clue.text: Ash, possibly, on edges of earthen dish

indicators.note: one piece placed on the other, coming after it in an across answer
the edges of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an ash is one example of a tree

explanation.surface: Ash, perhaps, round the rim of an earthenware dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges of' takes the outer letters of earthen, and 'on' sets the tree after them; 'possibly' marks ash as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a course served at a meal, the main course in America, is a dish.

clue.text: A British duty to arrange garb for streakers?

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A British obligation to sort out clothing for people who run naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrange' shuffles A BRITISH DUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke: streakers wear nothing, and bare skin, as on the day you were born, is their only outfit.

clue.text: Jam for bear

definitions.meaning: to jam is to become fixed and unable to move
to bear something is to tolerate or put up with it

explanation.surface: Preserves for an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one verb: to get stuck fast, and to endure (as in 'can't stand it').

clue.text: With pound coin (new design), reluctant to get minimal cover?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

indicators.note: a new design reshapes the coin, rearranging its letters

parts.note: loth means unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone with a freshly designed pound coin is unwilling to wear more than a scrap of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new design' rearranges COIN into OINC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth tied round the hips is about the least clothing anyone can wear, so a minimal cover.

clue.text: Making changes in device isn't encouraged

indicators.note: changes made to the letters put them in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Altering a gadget isn't something people are encouraged to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making changes' shuffles IN DEVICE ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone given a reward to act has been encouraged.

clue.text: Get drunk splitting French wine cask — I'm game!

indicators.note: the letters break the two other pieces apart by going between them

parts.note: vin is French for wine
a tun is a large cask

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy person breaking into a barrel of French wine declares they're up for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles Get, and 'splitting' lodges the result between wine and cask. The game is pontoon or blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game also called blackjack, its name French for twenty-one, is speaking here as a game.

clue.text: Golfer likely to need this accompaniment to fish, fried?

parts.note: chips go with fish in the classic British takeaway
food just out of the fryer is hot

explanation.surface: A golfer needing a side order with fried fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish and chips is the classic British takeaway. The split comes one letter later than the golf term.
explanation.definitionFit: A short lofted stroke onto the green is what a golfer near it is likely to need.

clue.text: No pressure for clemency after PM gets winning margin

indicators.note: the rest of the piece comes after the Prime Minister

parts.note: John Major was UK Prime Minister 1990-97

indicators.note: no pressure means the letter for pressure is removed

parts.note: pity means mercy or clemency
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A prime minister wins by a margin with no pressure to show mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major was a British prime minister. 'No' removes P from PITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the number of votes by which the winner beats the rest is the winning margin.

clue.text: Dreadfully sad judge popular on social media

parts.note: a judge hears a case
a topic is trending when widely discussed online

explanation.surface: A judge who has gone viral online, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: grief so deep it seems to tear the heart is dreadfully sad.

clue.text: Run through church chasing mole

indicators.note: the church follows the mole, coming after it

parts.note: a mole is a stone pier or breakwater
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A churchman chases a small burrowing animal while running through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' looks like the animal but is a harbour wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to run a blade through something is to pierce it.

clue.text: Rising models like to be drawn in suspended animation

indicators.note: the second piece is drawn into the first, sitting inside it
in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an artist's model sits for a portrait
as means like

explanation.surface: Models standing up to be sketched stay frozen in position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' is a verb, as sitters pose for artists; 'Rising' reads it upwards, and 'to be drawn in' takes like inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of no change or activity at all is a kind of suspended animation.

clue.text: Decorum — for devoutness, rector must be involved

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the rector is drawn inside, becoming involved in the other word

parts.note: piety is religious devoutness

explanation.surface: Good manners: a rector should take part in matters of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: proper, correct behaviour is decorum.

clue.text: Gunners tacitly agree to lift unhealthy gas

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting reads the word upwards

parts.note: a nod gives silent agreement

explanation.surface: Soldiers silently agree to clear away a harmful gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' turns NOD into DON.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the radioactive gas that seeps from rock and causes lung cancer is an unhealthy gas.

clue.text: Dickensian plot's unexpected turn

definitions.meaning: Oliver, the orphan of a Dickens novel, carries this surname
a surprise development in a story

explanation.surface: The surprising development in a Dickens storyline.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver is a Dickens hero, and a story's surprise development shares his surname.

clue.text: Mullet, say, discovered in fresh air, doomed

indicators.note: the letters are uncovered running across the words

explanation.surface: A grey mullet fish found in fresh air is doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mullet' is the haircut, short at the front and long at the back, not the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the mullet, short on top and long behind, is a style of haircut.

clue.text: Transport real and imaginary, not one for the birds

parts.note: a bus is real transport

indicators.note: not one means the letter for one is removed

parts.note: the TARDIS is the fictional time machine in Doctor Who, imaginary transport
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Vehicles real and fictional, not one fit for the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The TARDIS is the time-travelling police box from the BBC series Doctor Who. 'not' removes I from it, leaving TARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: large ground-dwelling game birds of open plains belong to the group named.

clue.text: Tiresome magistrates get used to it

definitions.meaning: magistrates spend their days hearing and judging cases in court

explanation.surface: Tedious work that magistrates become accustomed to.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome is a synonym; magistrates are used to judging cases, the court sense of the word.

clue.text: Monkey on board creating big problems

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside it, so the monkey sits within the letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the ship to be on board
a cheeky child, a little monkey, is a tinker

explanation.surface: A monkey on a ship causes serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the usual crossword way of saying inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang synonym: really difficult problems or tasks are stinkers.
